chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man whom he ordered to have his right hand cut off. So his left hand was presented, and they cut it off, and reckoned it as his right, and they said, 'We have only cut his left; should his right be cut off as well?' He said, 'His right hand would not be cut off, and his left has already been cut.'
And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who took an egg from the war booty, and they said, 'He has stolen, so cut him,' that, 'I would not cut anyone who has a share in what he has taken.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hand if the wrong hand is cut, or if the thief has a share in the stolen item?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) precise application of legal principles, demonstrating that the punishment for theft requires the specific intent and act of taking what is exclusively owned by another. In the first case, the mistaken cutting of the left hand is deemed sufficient due to the symmetry of the hands in this penalty, while the second case illustrates the concept of 'shirk' (shared ownership) in war booty, where taking a small item like an egg does not constitute theft because the taker has a legitimate share in the collective property.
